title: Chapter 18 – First Blood
html:
Lin Jian climbs the cliff with the Royal Spirit Chain folded in his sleeve and his Spirit Sense stretched thin ahead of him like a hand feeling along a dark wall. For the first two hundred paces the stain on the rock is easy to follow: a ragged line of pink, thin as watered wine, with a bloody handprint every ten steps where a man stopped to lean. After that the line grows fainter, and then it grows strange.

```
[Passive Trace]
Sample: dried fluid, cliff face, 3rd smear
Match: Gu Yan blood, 94%
Foreign compound: capsaicinoid (Mother's thread), present, diluted
Dilution trend: rising — subject is burning blood faster than it recovers
Estimated time since passage: 22 minutes
```

Twenty-two minutes. A man with broken ribs and pepper in his veins has moved a mile and a half through broken country. Every time Gu Yan burns what he has drunk, he runs faster and bleeds worse. The trail leads to a man running toward something that can mend him.

Hu said a Pool-stage man keeps one safe place, Lin Jian thinks. A den with a source.

He has no business following it. His mother's order still rings in his ears. If he goes on, the only thing between him and a cornered Pool-stage cultivator is a Qi Refining Fifth Stage body, a belt of nine pins, and a plan he does not have yet.

But Hu is dying slowly of a thing only Lin Jian can see. And the man who put it in him is up ahead, bleeding.

He keeps climbing.

* * *

The trail ends at a wall of ice.

A waterfall has frozen in mid-fall: a hundred feet of blue-white curtain, fat as a barn and hung with icicles as long as spears. Winter has not let go of the high ground. The pool at its foot is a ring of black rime. No path leads to it, no ledge, no footprint. The last pink handprint is on a boulder fifty paces downstream, and beyond it the trail simply stops.

Lin Jian stands among the spruce at the edge of the clearing, breathing through his mouth. His heart is a fist against his ribs. He does not step into the open.

Scan the ice.

```
[Structural Scan]
Target: frozen fall, face-on
Material: water ice, uniform, 99.2%
Anomaly: rear surface — cavity, depth 14 m, behind the third icicle cluster
Anomaly: ice thickness at left edge: 0.4 m, false-frozen (Qi-maintained, not natural)
Note: the ice at the left edge is a door.
```

A door, held shut by the Qi of a man who is bleeding out.

He watches for ten minutes. Then the third icicle cluster shivers, and a slow pink drop falls from the tip and freezes as it lands.

He sits on a root in the spruce and does what Hu has drilled into him: he counts what he has. The Royal Spirit Chain, one, folded. Six Flame-Burst slips, three of them with the old pepper charge, three of them plain. The Belt, nine pins, seven of them his own flawed seventy-eight-percent kind and two of them real. And in the cloth lining of the Belt, wrapped in a scrap of felt, the one thing he has told no one: his perfect pin. Ninety-nine percent, hand-made at the bench behind the granary with every cut exact, the single piece of work he is proud of.

A pin is a fixed point, he thinks. If I can find the place where his den stores its Qi, I do not need to hurt him. I need only give the den a different idea.

It is a thin plan. He steps out of the spruce and crosses the clearing at a crouch.

* * *

The ice door opens to a touch of Qi.

He feels it as he reaches for it: a faint, warm tug in his palm, like a fish nibbling at a line. The Sect's doors taste whoever stands before them and open for that blood alone. Lin Jian holds his hand flat against the left edge of the fall and does the only thing he can think of, which is nothing: a pond with no wind on it, a boy-shaped stone.

The ice grows thinner under his fingers. It cracks in a hair-fine line from top to bottom. A slab the width of a door peels away and falls inward with a soft, wet sound.

The cave behind is warm. That is the first wrong thing. After the cold of the clearing it hits his face like the breath of an animal, humid and coppery, and it smells of iron and old meat and sweet rot. Light comes from ahead: a deep, throbbing crimson. It swells and fades and swells, in a slow rhythm like a heartbeat.

He edges into the tunnel with one hand on the wall.

The passage bends twice and opens into a round chamber the size of the Lin great hall. In the exact center, hanging from a chain, is a lamp: a bowl of bone the size of a washbasin, rimmed with teeth, its mouth full of some crimson fluid that burns without flame, and the light that comes off it is not the light of fire. It is the color of a cut. It spills down in a column onto the floor, onto a pool, and the pool is a spiral.

A spiral. A long, shallow channel carved into the stone in a tightening coil, four turns around, each turn a hand's breadth deep and filled to the brim with blood. Not fresh blood. Black-red, slow, thick, full of tiny floating motes that flicker like embers. The whole thing turns, very slowly, one revolution every few breaths, and the lamp's light turns with it.

In the center of the spiral lies Gu Yan.

* * *

He is on his back in the middle channel with his head on a stone pillow and his arms flung wide. The Crimson Vulture Cloak is a ruin around him. The oiled-silk veil lies torn on the floor. Mother's rogue's knife is still in his side to the hilt, and the cloth around it is dark with wet, and when he breathes, the breath whistles.

Lin Jian goes very still.

The spiral is feeding him. He can see it. The blood in the channels creeps toward the center, thread by thread, and where the threads touch Gu Yan's skin they sink in and disappear, and the man's face grows a shade less gray with each revolution of the coil. The pink in the veins of his throat is changing, shifting slowly toward red.

Every few breaths, a single thread of the blood that sinks into Gu Yan comes out again at his thigh, at the pinprick where Mother's water thread went in, in a thin pale trickle. The coil is mending him. The pepper is un-mending him. It is a race, and the pepper is not losing.

Scan it. The whole thing.

```
[Structural Scan — Formation]
Target: Blood-Spiral Basin (Yellow Grade, 4-turn)
Function: draws stored blood Qi inward toward a single anchor (the occupant)
Anchor: occupant's Qi signature (keyed to Gu Yan, 100%)
Input: bone lamp (blood-oil reservoir, ~40 L), drains slowly
Structural note: spiral channels are cut with 16 relay notches along the outer turn; notch 9 is cracked
Weakness: relay chain is directional. Reverse the keyed anchor and the flow reverses.
Cost to Separate a notch (Level 2, non-living stone/blood-oil): 6 CE
WARNING: subject is within 4 m. Qi-sense detection probability: 71%.
```

Reverse the anchor.

The basin draws blood toward the man it knows. If the flow ran the other way, it would pull blood out of him, and a man bleeding pepper from a dozen holes could not stop it.

But the anchor is keyed to Gu Yan's Qi. What Lin Jian can change is where the channel thinks the anchor is.

He turns his eyes to the notches.

Sixteen of them, evenly spaced along the outer coil like the markings on a clock. Notch nine has a hairline crack. If a pin were driven into that crack, the relay would close on the pin instead of the stone, and a pin, he knows, is nothing but a very stubborn anchor. A pin does not have a Qi signature. It has a shape. And the shape of his perfect pin is, for the purposes of a Yellow Grade basin, a better anchor than a dying man's heart.

Notch nine. Then the basin pulls toward the pin, not toward him.

It is eleven paces to notch nine, across an open floor, past a man who has spent his life listening for exactly this kind of footfall.

He takes the first step.

* * *

"Radish," says Gu Yan.

The voice is soft, almost fond. Gu Yan has not opened his eyes. His lips barely move.

Lin Jian's foot hangs a finger's width above the stone. He does not put it down.

"Don't stop on my account." The right eye opens. It is red-rimmed and bloodshot and calm. "Come. Sit. I won't hurt you. I can't, you see." He lifts one hand a finger's width off the stone and lets it fall. "I am in no shape to hurt anyone. The woman made sure of that."

Lin Jian says nothing. His hand is already inside his sleeve.

"The steward told me about you." Gu Yan's smile is a thin line. "The one with the little boy who counts everything. 'Watch the child,' he said. 'He's the clever one. The rest of them are stone.' I thought he was exaggerating. A steward from a dying clan, wanting to be clever for his betters." The eye drifts to the Belt at Lin Jian's waist. "Nine pins. That is a good belt. Is it his?" He nods toward the dark. "The smith's?"

Zhao Bei, Lin Jian thinks. The Red Ridge steward. The one who paid with three hundred low stones, and who sent a message to a man he'd never met about a boy he'd never spoken to. Zhao Bei told him to watch me. How does a steward in Red Ridge know I count?

He does not let it show on his face.

"You came after me," Gu Yan says. "That is either very brave or very stupid." A cough shakes him. A fresh stream of pink slides from the corner of his mouth. "I have decided I prefer stupid. Stupid children make mistakes. Come closer, radish. I want to see your face."

He takes his hand out of his sleeve with a Flame-Burst slip pinched between two fingers, and throws.

It is not aimed at Gu Yan. It strikes the bone lamp's chain a hand above the bowl, and the slip bursts in a flat white crack. The pepper-charged flame spreads through the fumes of the blood-oil, and the whole chamber flares orange. The lamp swings. Hot ash rains down.

Gu Yan's head snaps up. "You—"

Lin Jian is already running.

* * *

Eleven paces. He covers them in six.

Cloudstep carries him over the first channel with a flick of his heel. He lands on the rim of the second turn, a hand's breadth wide, with blood sliding past on both sides. Behind him, Gu Yan is trying to rise.

Notch nine is a hand's breadth from his boot. A hairline crack in the stone, running diagonal across the rim. He drops to one knee, pulls the felt-wrapped pin from the lining of his Belt, and unrolls it.

It is only an iron needle with a groove, no longer than his hand, but it hums in his fingers. Hu, when he first held it, said nothing for a full minute and then handed it back as if it were hot.

"No," says Gu Yan. The word is flat, and sudden, and it has something in it Lin Jian has not heard before. "No. Put that down."

He drives the pin into the crack with the heel of his hand.

Nothing happens.

For one long breath, nothing happens at all. The lamp swings. The spiral turns. Gu Yan has pushed himself onto his elbow, face contorted, mist beginning to leak from the folds of his cloak in thin red threads. The knife in his side has come half out. He reaches for it.

Then the stone sings.

It is a high, thin, descending note, like a wet finger run round the lip of a bowl. The pin glows pale blue. The crack around it widens and closes and widens again, and Lin Jian feels, in his teeth and his spine, the relay chain turn over, like a great wheel catching a new tooth.

The blood in the channels stops.

It hangs, black-red and shivering, for the length of a heartbeat. Then it begins to flow the other way.

* * *

Gu Yan screams.

It is the scream of a man who has had one kind of pain for an hour and is suddenly given another. The threads of blood that were going in are coming out. They lift from his skin, from the wound at his side, from the pinprick in his thigh, from the pores of his face, and they slide down toward the channel, and the channel takes them in. The red mist of his cloak shreds like wet paper. He claws at the stone and finds no purchase. The basin has stopped loving him.

He rolls, and half-rises, and for a moment his one good eye finds Lin Jian across the coil.

"I am going to eat you," Gu Yan says, in a whisper that carries.

He lunges.

He is on his feet, somehow. The mist is the color of rust, and it moves with him, and the curved blade, the bone-pale blade with the nick near the guard, is in his hand though Lin Jian never saw him draw it. He crosses the coil in one leap, over the middle channel, red cloak spreading, and Lin Jian sees the edge swing down at his throat and knows, with perfect clarity, that he cannot dodge it.

He does not try.

He crushes the Royal Spirit Chain in his left fist.

Gold-white light bursts through his fingers. The talisman flares and spins out of his hand and unfolds in the air: a ring of linked glowing loops that falls over Gu Yan like a net. The blade stops a hand's breadth from Lin Jian's collarbone.

One.

The chain goes taut. The mist screams against it. Gu Yan's whole body locks in the air, mid-lunge, arms flung wide, jaw clenched, the blade vibrating in his fist. He is a Pool-stage cultivator. Father drew it to hold a Qi Refining boy for six breaths. It will not hold a Pool-stage man that long.

Two.

It cracks. A thread of light snaps away from the ring.

Three.

Lin Jian rolls sideways, off the rim, and drops into the channel. The blood is warm around his shins, thick as paint. He can feel it pulling at him. The basin has not decided whose blood it wants. He wades. Five steps to the anchor pillar at the foot of the lamp. He has marked it: a squat stone column, as thick as a man's waist, set where the four turns of the spiral meet. The lamp's chain runs through it.

Four.

The chain screams. Another link goes. Gu Yan's blade has begun to drift, a hand's breadth at a time, toward his own throat.

Lin Jian reaches the pillar. He draws a second pin from the Belt, a flawed one, seventy-eight percent, and sets it against the stone at the point where the lamp chain enters. He does not drive it. He holds it, and he looks at the pillar, and thinks very clearly, in the voice he uses for the work:

Separate.

```
[Separation]
Target: bone-lamp chain anchor (stone / blood-oil residue)
Operation: isolate iron alloy from chain link 1
Result: CHAIN LINK DROPPED
Cost: 6 CE (remaining: 35 / 400)
```

The link falls away in his hand as a pinch of gray dust. The lamp's chain, held by that single link, gives a sudden, heavy lurch.

Five.

The bone bowl drops.

It falls forty feet. It hits the center of the spiral with a crash like a bell dropped on a flagstone, and the forty liters of blood-oil in it go up in a sheet of crimson fire. The flame is not hot; it burns cold and wet. It races across the coil, and into the channels, and into the blood that is running backward through them, and the pepper in the blood, the pepper that has been eating Gu Yan from the inside for an hour, meets the fire.

Six.

The chain breaks.

* * *

Gu Yan does not scream this time.

There is no breath left in him for it. He hits the floor on his knees, blade falling from his hand with a clang, and the mist that comes out of him is not red anymore. It is pale pink, nearly white, and it comes out in great ragged sheets, like steam from a stove. He claws at his own chest. He claws at the knife in his side. Every vein in his throat is standing out like cord.

"Smith," he says, hoarse. "Tell the smith... it was not..."

His voice breaks. He tries again.

"The boy," he says. "The boy. Tell the steward—"

He does not finish it.

He falls forward on his face. For a long moment, the cave is quiet except for the cold fire hissing in the channels. The spiral is slowing. The blood in it is thickening and going dark.

Lin Jian stands at the foot of the pillar with his chest heaving. The numbness comes up through his legs like cold water, and for a long, empty moment he waits for it to turn into something.

It does not.

I killed him.

He does not use a blade. He does not use a talisman. He uses a pin and a link of chain and the one great, ugly, honest truth Hu has drilled into him since the day they met: everything is held by something; find the something.

I killed him, and the thing in my stomach is hunger.

He sits down on the rim and puts his head on his knees for sixty breaths. Then he gets up, because there is work.

Scan the body.

```
[Scan — Remains]
Subject: Gu Yan, Pool Stage 3rd, deceased
Cause: exsanguination (Qi-reverse), compound toxicity (capsaicinoid)
Loot candidates (see below)
Blood-Draw technique residue — structure partially legible. +14 CE (noted)
```

On the belt: a pouch of Sect-stamped leather. Inside are six low-grade spirit stones, a vial of rust-colored powder that smells of copper, a scrap of talisman paper with a half-finished glyph, and a folded map of the Hollow country in a tidy hand.

The pouch he leaves. He puts everything back and sets the pouch on the dead man's chest. Grandfather will want to see the cave exactly as it was.

The curved blade he picks up, carefully, by the flat. The nick near the guard is a shallow notch the length of a grain of rice. On the tang, where the wrapping has slid, he can make out a stamp no larger than a thumbnail: a hammer, and beneath it, a wave.

Hu's mark.

He wraps the blade in the dead man's torn veil and sets it by the pouch, next to the body.

And last, the thing he does not expect.

Under the cloak, beneath the left arm, sewn into the lining: a flat, palm-sized plate of black metal, not iron, not steel, with a thin band of fine script running round its edge in a language he does not know. It is warm. It hums.

```
[Scan — Unknown Artifact]
Material: unclassified. Not in local database.
Partial structural match: Heavenly Artificer Fragment, 4.2%
Origin: unknown
Condition: broken edge, 1 of ≥3 pieces
CE gain on scan: +62.
Note: this fragment contains a partial recursion. It may be related to ARK-7's own schematics.
```

Lin Jian does not breathe.

A Blood Shadow assassin carried it, he thinks. To sell? To keep? Or because the Sect knows what it is?

He tucks it inside his shirt, against his skin. It is the only thing from that cave he takes.

```
[CE Update]
Scans logged this session: cliff trace, ice door, basin, remains, fragment.
Gain: +95 CE (total: 130 / 400)
Level 2 → Level 3 requires 200 CE and a Qi Refining Eighth Stage body.
Notice: Level 3 unlocks living-tissue Separation and basic mechanical locks. (Not yet available.)
```

He stares at the last line. Living tissue. He has seen the word, and he has known what it meant, and he has not let himself think it.

The fire is out. The spiral has gone black and still.

He leaves.

* * *

Something grips his ankle as he steps out of the ice door.

It is cold, and quick, and he nearly screams. He looks down, and the stone is bare, and the clearing is empty, and for a moment he thinks he has imagined it. Then he sees the mark.

On the skin of his left ankle, just above the boot, a band of gray has bloomed. It is the shape of a hand: four long fingers and a thumb, wrapped round the bone. It does not hurt. It is not cold anymore. It is only gray, and dry, like the skin of a mummy, as though something had held him there for a moment and let go.

The basin, he thinks. When I waded the channel.

He tries to rub it off. It does not smudge. He pulls his trouser leg over it, and tucks the cuff into his boot.

Later.

He climbs down the cliff.

* * *

They meet him in the pines.

Su Qinghe is first. She comes through the trees at a dead run with her sleeves rolled to the elbow and her hands still stained, and she stops three paces from him as if she has hit a wall. Behind her are Feng, with his long blade drawn and Kai at his shoulder, and Dong with a lit lantern he does not need, and a half-dozen of the Lin guards, strung out along the slope.

She looks at her son from his hair to his boots. She takes in the blood to the thighs, the pale face, the hands.

"I told you to run for the gate," she says.

"Yes, Mother."

"You did not."

"No."

She does not strike him. She does not shout. She steps in and puts both hands on his shoulders, and holds him there, hard enough that her nails go through the cloth, and for one breath her whole face does something he has never seen it do.

"Is he dead?" she says.

"Yes."

"Where?"

"In the cave behind the frozen fall. The ice door is open." His voice is steady, which surprises him. "His blood-spiral is dead too. The lamp fell. There is a pouch on the body. I left everything where it was."

"How, Jian?"

He does not answer for a moment. Then, as lightly as he can: "He was very hurt. His own formation turned on him, in the end."

It is not a lie. It is not the whole truth either.

Feng has come up behind his sister-in-law. He says nothing. His eyes go to Lin Jian's boots, to the hem of his trousers, and stay there. For one long second, Lin Jian is sure he has seen the gray band. Then Feng looks up, and meets his eyes, and his face tells him nothing at all. He turns, and gives a short low order, and two of the guards go loping up the trail toward the ice.

"Kai," Feng says. "Dong. Stay with him."

"Yes, Uncle."

"How is Hu?" Lin Jian asks.

It is Su Qinghe who answers. Her voice has gone very quiet.

"He is alive," she says. "Your grandfather's healer has seen him. She says the wound is clean. She says she does not understand why it will not close."

"I do."

She looks at him.

"It's the blade," he says. "It's the same Qi that was in his old wound. The cut is feeding the residue. I can help."

"How?"

"The poultice. I have a way to clean it." He swallows. "It will take all night."

His mother holds his eyes, and he can see her weighing it: the child, the night, the lie she has already decided to let him tell. She does not ask a second time how he knows. She only nods, once, and takes her hands from his shoulders.

"Then we should go," she says.

* * *

He does not sleep.

Hu lies on his pallet in the forge loft, gray as ash, the wound on his side wrapped in strips of Su Qinghe's best cloth. His breathing is shallow and wet. Beside him on the table sits a bowl of the Lin healer's poultice, a green-black paste of herbs and spirit-ash, and beside the bowl, a blade. Not the curved one. That one is in the cave, where it belongs. This is the simple iron knife Lin Jian has carried since the Hollow.

He sets the bowl before him and puts one hand flat on its rim.

Scan.

```
[Scan — Poultice]
Target: Lin healer's Meridian-binding poultice, 180 g
Contaminant: Blood-Shadow residue, absorbed from Hu's wound, 3.4%
Effect: poultice binds residue to tissue, keeps wound open
Recommended action: SEPARATE contaminant
Cost: 4 CE per 60 g. Total: 12 CE (remaining: 118 / 400)
```

Twelve points. He has spent twelve points on strangers and strays and old men before. He pays them without a thought.

Separate.

The paste in the bowl trembles. A fine gray scum rises to the surface, and he skims it off with the back of a spoon and drops it in the fire, where it hisses and dies. He lays the cleansed paste on a clean cloth and carries it to the pallet.

Hu's eye opens. It is cloudy and unfocused.

"Boy."

"Rest, Hu."

"The poultice." The voice is thin as thread. "It tastes... different."

"It's the same one. I only strained it."

A long silence. The old man's lips move in something that could be a smile. His hand finds Lin Jian's wrist, and the grip is weak but certain.

"Strained it," Hu says. "Of course you did."

He lets go. His eye closes.

Lin Jian applies the poultice, wrap by wrap, with careful fingers. He changes the dressing at midnight, and at the third hour, and at the fifth. Each time the scum is a little thinner. Each time, the black thread in the wound recedes a little more. By the time the sky outside the loft window turns the color of pewter, the old man's breathing has steadied, and the wound at his side is no longer weeping.

He sits back on his heels, light-headed. His hands are shaking.

Behind him, a board creaks.

He turns.

Feng stands in the doorway of the loft, one hand on the frame. He is out of his armor. He wears only his plain gray shirt, and his hair is loose, and for a man who has not slept either, he looks very calm. He looks at Hu. He looks at the empty bowl. Then he looks, with no change in his face at all, at the hem of Lin Jian's left trouser leg, where it has ridden up over the boot.

The gray band is plain in the lamplight. Four long fingers and a thumb.

Neither of them speaks.

Then Feng says, in the tone one uses to remark on the weather, "Your grandfather asks for you at first light."

"Yes, Uncle."

"Tell him exactly what you saw. Not what you did."

He turns to go. At the head of the stairs he pauses, and without looking back, he says:

"Whatever you left in that cave, leave it there. Whatever you took out of it, keep it close. And tell no one, not even your father, what is on your ankle until you know what it is."

He goes down. His steps fade.

Lin Jian sits in the dawn light with his back against the cold forge wall, and a dying man's breathing in his ears, and the black fragment warm against his chest. For a moment, nothing in the world is moving.

Then, very softly, in the quiet of his head, something chimes.

```
[Notice]
Fragment resonance detected. Recursion active.
Compatibility with ARK-7 schematics: unknown. Further scans required.
```

He stares at the words until the sun comes up.
